title: Beatrix and the Typewriter
premise: In 1899, in the river town of Vellum Falls, Beatrix Dunmore works her father's print shop while revolution simmers across the bridge in the capital. When the bridge closes for winter, the town becomes a pressure cooker of spies, pamphlets, and loyalties, and Beatrix discovers she can move messages no one else can — through the very type she sets. As the century turns, the family must decide who takes the last berth on the final barge out: her father, whose presses are wanted by both sides; her brother, who has joined the rebels; or Beatrix herself, whom history has quietly chosen. In the end, Beatrix sends them both and stays behind, printing the true account of the revolution under a name that is finally, entirely her own.
about_author: Marguerite Voss is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print equipment in workshop museums across Europe. Her novels explore the people behind historical machinery — hands, ink, and the quiet decisions that turn eras.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. We meet the Dunmore print shop: her father Aldous cutting typefaces, her brother Casper restless for the capital, Beatrix content in the rhythm of the composing stick. A customer leaves a pamphlet too dangerous to print. Emotional beat: cozy routine shadowed by the first tremor of change.

chapters.title: Iron Across the Water
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The bridge closes for the season with an official proclamation; Casper watches soldiers take positions and realizes the closure is not weather but strategy. He hides his sympathy for the workers' committees from his family. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of a secret.

chapters.title: What the Type Remembers
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Setting type late at night, Beatrix finds hidden instructions embedded in a confiscated manuscript's kerning — coded orders between factions. She realizes typography itself is carrying the revolution's secrets, and she is the only one literate enough in it to read them. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovery.

chapters.title: The Committee of Ink
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Both sides come calling: the governor wants the press for propaganda, the rebels want pamphlets. Aldous stalls, playing printer-neutral, but accepts rebel money he tells himself is just business. Emotional beat: a good man learning how compromise curdles.

chapters.title: Winter of Pamphlets
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Printing by candlelight, Beatrix becomes the rebellion's anonymous voice while officially serving the governor. Casper discovers her hand in the pamphlets and joins the cause openly, straining against their father's caution. Emotional beat: sister and brother conspiring, power intoxicating her.

chapters.title: A Name Not Hers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The governor's men trace a pamphlet's typeface to the Dunmore shop. To save the family, Casper claims sole authorship and is arrested. Beatrix learns her words have consequences written in someone else's blood. Emotional beat: guilt as identity fractures.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She trades the coded correspondence she decoded — proof implicating the governor's own officers — for Casper's release, making herself valuable to both sides and trusted by neither. Aldous discovers what she's done and what she's become. Emotional beat: power gained, innocence lost.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. The ice breaks early; a rebel barge will make one crossing before fighting reaches the town, with room for only one passenger. Aldous must choose, and realizes Beatrix has already outgrown every choice he could make for her. Emotional beat: a father's reckoning.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the dock, Beatrix puts her father and Casper aboard together, forging the manifest so the berth reads as one man. Gunfire begins upriver as the barge pulls away. She walks back to the shop through smoke. Emotional beat: the climax — love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: Set in Her Own Type
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Under the new year, Beatrix prints the true chronicle of the closed bridge under her own name, distributing it as the town changes hands. Years later, a copy reaches her father abroad, set in a typeface she cut herself. Emotional beat: resolution — identity claimed, truth outlasting power.
